current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024-2025 (221st Legislature) and 2026-2027 (222nd) through 2026-08-18. Governing law: Open Public Records Act, N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1 et seq., fee section N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5, last amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2 (enacted 2024-06-05, effective 2024-09-03). Codified text opened from the Legislature's official statutes download (STATUTES-TEXT.zip, updated 2026-08-18); its history line ends '2024, c.16, s.2' — no 2025 or 2026 amendment. Chapter law and S2930 [2R] markup opened: P.L.2024, c.16 kept the flat $0.05/$0.07 duplication rate, DELETED the sentence allowing agencies to charge a demonstrated higher actual duplication cost, added the itemized-list/objection/rebuttable-presumption provisions to 47:1A-5(c), the website-direction no-fee rule and 2x-cost physical-copy ceiling in 5(e), the commercial-purpose 14-day window and 2x-cost expedite fee in 5(i)(1), and the 14-business-day retrieval window. GRC rules N.J.A.C. 5:105 (readopted 2022-11-07) carry no fee content. GRC guidance: Custodian's Handbook 8th ed. (Jan 2025) is post-amendment and current; the official request form (2024-9-3) is current; the custodian FAQ page and 2011 Toolkit are partly pre-2024 (FAQ still describes the deleted actual-cost override and an older model form's deposit percentages) — guidance-vs-law gap flagged where relied on. Municipal scope: OPRA binds all 'public agencies' including political subdivisions; no separate agency-only schedule; municipal ordinances cannot alter OPRA fees (GRC).

resolutions.unit: USD per page (letter size or smaller | legal size or larger)
resolutions.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(b)(1), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
resolutions.notes: Mandatory flat rate ('shall be'), not a ceiling. P.L.2024, c.16 DELETED the former sentence permitting an agency to charge a demonstrated higher actual duplication cost, so no municipal ordinance or actual-cost calculation may raise the rate (GRC Handbook 8th ed.: 'P.L. 2024, c.16 removed consideration of calculating an actual cost exceeding the foregoing copying costs'). Exceptions: fees 'otherwise provided by law or regulation' for specific record types (e.g., N.J.S.A. 39:4-131 accident reports add up to $5 for non-in-person requests); GRC FAQ: municipal ordinances do not qualify as such law/regulation. Applies to every 'public agency', which by N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 includes political subdivisions (municipalities).

resolutions.notes: No separate color rate exists in OPRA, N.J.A.C. 5:105 or GRC guidance. The statutory page rate governs printed matter irrespective of color. Where the record 'cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size', 47:1A-5(c) permits an additional special service charge based on actual direct cost (NJ-M06). The pre-2024 GRC actual-cost calculation that separated color copiers (OPRA Alert Vol.3 Iss.2) is obsolete after P.L.2024, c.16.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (legal size page 'or larger'); plus special service charge at actual direct cost where the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary copying equipment in ordinary business size
resolutions.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(b)(1) and (c), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger. ... Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
resolutions.manual_verification: The $0.07 tier is stated as 'legal size page or larger'; large-format reproduction (plans, maps) typically triggers 5(c) 'cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size' — confirm treatment per city.
resolutions.notes: Statutory page rate covers 'legal size page or larger' at $0.07; oversized/nonstandard reproduction beyond ordinary equipment is priced by the 5(c) special service charge (actual direct cost, reasonable, itemized, requestor may object before it is incurred). No fixed oversized rate is set anywhere.

resolutions.value: actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies (special service charge), reasonable
resolutions.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c) and (d), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
resolutions.source_language: Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable. The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges. The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
resolutions.notes: Specialty reproduction (photos, maps, transcripts, media conversion) is chargeable only as a 'special service charge' (printed matter, 5(c)) or 'special service fee' (medium/format conversion, 5(d)) 'based upon the actual direct cost' and 'reasonable', in addition to the statutory duplication fee; must be itemized and explained; requestor may review and object before it is incurred; presumed reasonable with burden on requestor. GRC 14-point analysis is the guideline for reasonableness.

new_rules.legal_concept: Flat statutory duplication rate — actual-cost override repealed
new_rules.atomic_rule: As amended by P.L.2024, c.16, the public agency shall assess $0.05 per letter-size-or-smaller page and $0.07 per legal-size-or-larger page for duplication of printed matter, and may no longer charge a demonstrated higher actual cost of duplication (the former override sentence was deleted).
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Request for paper copies of a government record embodied in printed matter; no other law or regulation prescribes a record-specific fee
new_rules.source_language: Enacted text: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger. || Text deleted by P.L.2024, c.16 (bracketed in S2930 [2R]): [If a public agency can demonstrate that its actual costs for duplication of a government record exceed the foregoing rates, the public agency shall be permitted to charge the actual cost of duplicating the record. The actual cost of duplicating the record, upon which all copy fees are based, shall be the cost of materials and supplies used to make a copy of the record, but shall not include the cost of labor or other overhead expenses associated with making the copy except as provided for in subsection c. of this section.] || GRC Handbook 8th ed.: Custodians must charge a flat rate of $0.05 per letter size (8 ½” x 11”) page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size (8 ½” x 14”) page or larger, if providing a requestor with paper copies. Note that P.L. 2024, c.16 removed consideration of calculating an “actual cost” exceeding the foregoing copying costs.

new_rules.legal_concept: Special service charge computation basis (GRC guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A special service charge under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c) is computed at the hourly rate of the lowest-level employee capable of fulfilling the request, without fringe benefits, on a case-by-case basis, and may not be established in advance by ordinance.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Custodian assesses a special service charge for an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort
new_rules.source_language: Actual direct cost means hourly rate of the lowest level employee capable of fulfilling the request (no fringe benefits). A special service charge is calculated on a case-by-case basis. No special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance. || Toolkit response template: [Identify lowest level employee capable of fulfilling the request, their direct hourly rate (minus fringe benefits), the number of hours anticipated to complete request and the total estimated special service charge]. Kindly respond in writing with your acceptance or rejection of this estimated charge. We will not begin to process this request until we receive your written acceptance.
new_rules.source_authority: GRC Custodian's Handbook, 8th ed. (Jan 2025) p.27; GRC Custodian's Toolkit (2011) response template; GRC Special Service Charge 14-point analysis
new_rules.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)

Super. 61 (App. Div. 2008) as cited by GRC. Handbook cautions its analysis 'may change given the new rebuttal standard' of P.L.2024, c.16.

new_rules.atomic_rule: A requestor has 14 business days to retrieve the government records after the custodian gives notice that the request has been completed and the records are available.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Custodian notifies requestor that the request is completed and records are available
new_rules.source_language: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following notice from the custodian that the request has been completed and the records are available.
new_rules.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2

new_rules.atomic_rule: Where the requestor agrees to pay an assessed special service charge, the custodian is not required to provide access until the requestor has remitted payment; if the requestor objects and refuses to pay, the custodian may deny the request; per the GRC form, an accepted special service charge may require a deposit or payment in full before reproduction and the balance is due upon delivery.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Fee/special service charge assessed and accepted (or refused) by requestor
new_rules.source_language: GRC Handbook: If the requestor objects to the special service charge and refuses to pay it, the custodian may deny the request for access to the record. However, if the requestor is willing to pay for it, the custodian is not required to provide access until the requestor has remitted payment. || GRC form: The custodian may require a deposit against costs for reproducing documents whenever the custodian anticipates that the documents requested will cost in excess of $5 to reproduce. N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(f). Where a special service charge is warranted under OPRA, that amount will be communicated to you as required under the statute. You have the opportunity to review and object to the charge prior to it being incurred. If, however, you approve of the fact and amount of the special service charge, you may be required to pay a deposit or pay in full prior to reproduction of the documents. You may be charged a prepayment or deposit when a request for copies exceeds $5.00. The custodian will contact you and advise you of any deposit requirements. You agree to pay the balance due upon delivery of the records.

new_rules.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of media = purchase price of the material, no labor (GRC guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The 'actual cost' chargeable for supplies used to provide electronic records (flash drives, CDs, DVDs, tapes) is the specific fee the agency paid to purchase the material; e-mail and fax delivery are free.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Records provided on a physical electronic medium
new_rules.source_language: Records provided via e-mail and facsimile are free of charge. However, custodians may charge for the actual cost to provide access to electronic records on supplies such as flash drives, CDs, DVDs, videotapes, audiotapes, etc. The “actual cost” is the specific fee the agency paid to purchase the materials. For example, if the GRC purchased a package of 100 CD-ROMs for $100 and provided records to a requestor on 1 CD-ROM, the actual cost of said CD-ROM is $1.00 ($100 ÷ 100 = $1.00).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (GRC Custodian's Handbook, Eighth Edition, January 2025 — post-P.L.2024, c.16 guidance)
new_rules.notes: Also stated in OPRA Alert Vol.3 Iss.2 (Nov 2010) and GRC FAQ ('cannot include any labor fees').

new_rules.legal_concept: Municipal ordinances cannot set OPRA copy fees or special service charges (GRC guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A municipal ordinance is not a 'law or regulation' that can prescribe a different OPRA copy fee, and no special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance; the statutory rate and case-by-case special service charge govern.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Municipality purports to set OPRA copy or special service fees by ordinance
new_rules.source_language: GRC FAQ: Municipal ordinances do not qualify under OPRA as being another law or regulation. || GRC Handbook: No special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual postage recoverable for mailed delivery (GRC guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian must grant access by the delivery method the requestor requests (regular mail, e-mail, fax) and may charge the associated actual costs, i.e., actual postage.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Requestor asks for delivery by mail
new_rules.source_language: A custodian must grant access to a government record by the method of delivery requested (regular mail, e-mail, or fax). Custodians may charge associated costs for same (i.e. actual postage costs). || GRC form: [Payment Information box, column text as printed] Fees: Letter size pages - $0.05 per page Legal size pages - $0.07 per page Other materials (CD, DVD, etc) – actual cost of material Delivery: Delivery / postage fees additional depending upon delivery type. Extras: Special service charge dependent upon request.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver is discretionary; no statutory exemption from fees (GRC guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: No one is exempt from OPRA fees by statute (other than the statutory no-fee categories); providing records free of charge is at the custodian's discretion.
new_rules.trigger_conditions: Requestor asks for fees to be waived
new_rules.source_language: Nothing in OPRA exempts anyone from having to pay the requisite fees to obtain government records. If a custodian wants to provide records to any person free of charge, it is at the custodian's discretion.

new_rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification (GRC custodian FAQ page is undated and partly pre-dates P.L.2024, c.16; the quoted statement is not contradicted by the 2024 amendments)

applicability_notes: OPRA's fee provisions (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5) bind every 'public agency', which N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 defines to include 'any political subdivision of the State ... and any division, board, bureau, office, commission or other instrumentality within or created by a political subdivision' — municipalities are directly bound; there is no separate state-agency-only schedule. All statutory rows: applies_to = all_public_bodies.

Municipalities have NO local discretion over the per-page rate: the rate is a mandatory flat 'shall be' figure, P.L.2024, c.16 deleted the actual-cost override, and GRC guidance holds that municipal ordinances are not the 'law or regulation' that can prescribe a different fee and that special service charges cannot be pre-set by ordinance.

Special record fees 'otherwise provided by law or regulation' override the OPRA rate for those records only (e.g., N.J.S.A. 39:4-131 accident reports — municipal police; N.J.S.A. 40:55D-12(c) 200-foot property-owner list at up to $0.25 per name or $10, whichever is greater — municipal administrative officer; N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5.3(c)-(d) enumerated election records free of charge from 'election agencies' which include Municipal Clerks). These are record-specific and outside the 36 general items.

GRC guidance rows (Handbook 8th ed. 2025, form 2024-9-3, Toolkit 2011, FAQ undated) are Official Guidance/Official Form, not law; the FAQ page still describes the pre-2024 actual-cost override and an older model form's 50%/100% deposit language — flagged wherever relied on.
material_negatives: No hourly labor rate, billing increment, free-labor-hours, periodic free-time, overhead percentage (beyond 'actual direct cost'/'no fringe'), or numeric labor threshold anywhere in OPRA, N.J.A.C. 5:105 or GRC guidance — labor is chargeable only through the qualitative 5(c)/5(d) special service charge gates.

No estimate-response window, revised-estimate variance trigger, estimate validity period, deposit percentage cap, nonpayment-withdrawal period, prior-debt prepayment rule, deposit-clock tolling rule, de-minimis floor, minimum fee, certification fee, or electronic-payment requirement in NJ law or guidance.

No general fee-waiver provision (indigence/public interest); only category-based no-fee rules (crime victims, electronic/non-printed materials, website-directed requests, certain election records) plus GRC guidance that waiver is at the custodian's discretion.
No commercial-purpose surcharge on ordinary fees; the only commercial fee is the optional 7-day expedite special service fee capped at 2x cost of production.
No graduated page bands or free page allowance (former bands repealed 2010; flat rate mandatory since P.L.2010, c.75; actual-cost override deleted by P.L.2024, c.16).
N.J.A.C. 5:105 (GRC rules) contains no fee, deposit or special-service-charge provisions.

No 2025-2026 amendment to N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5: official codified history line ends '2024, c.16, s.2'; GRC's readable OPRA is 'as of September 3, 2024' with no later version posted as of this research date.
gaps_manual_verification: GRC custodian FAQ page (undated) still states the pre-2024 actual-cost override and references an older model form's '50% or other deposit when a request for copies exceeds $25' / '100% for anonymous requests over $5' — superseded by the 2024 form and P.L.2024, c.16 for the rate; verify GRC has not applied a deposit percentage in post-2024 decisions.

Whether the 7/14-business-day response clock tolls while a deposit or special service charge acceptance is outstanding is a GRC-decision question, not statutory text — verify before configuring a tolling effect.

Color and oversized copies: the statute prices all 'printed matter' by page size only; whether color output or large-format reproduction triggers the 5(c) special service charge is a per-request determination — human review before configuring a color rate other than $0.05/$0.07.
Municipal certification fees: no OPRA or general municipal statute found; any local certification fee needs a non-OPRA legal basis — human legal review.
